headline: Across media, gaming, publishing and education firms are investing in AI while revenue trends diverge.
summary: Media & Entertainment shows strong top‑line growth at Disney but mixed IT spending signals. Gaming firms report modest revenue with Brightstar expanding tech spend and others uncertain. Publishing mixes positive AI moves at Pearson with a revenue miss at Scholastic. Education players are broadly positive, highlighted by AI and quantum initiatives at NYU and Pearson.

industries.summary: Disney posted $25,248 m revenue and a 22% operating margin, driving a upbeat tone. WBD/Skydance and Versant also reported positive results, though Skydance signaled tighter IT spend. Cox and LA Times offered no clear financial data.

leaders.why: Largest revenue and strong operating margin

themes.title: AI talent acquisition
themes.detail: Disney is spending $180 m to hire staff from Character.AI and allocating $60 m annually for the workforce.

themes.title: AI‑driven content
themes.detail: Skydance is investing heavily in AI‑generated content and partnering with Google for generative news features.

themes.title: Platform rebuilds
themes.detail: Versant’s Fandango unit is moving into original programming, indicating digital platform investment.

industries.it_note: IT spend is expanding at Disney, tightening at Skydance, and unclear for Cox and LA Times.

industries.summary: Revenue ranges from $584 m at Brightstar to $828 m at Light & Wonder. Bally’s shows strong growth, while Brightstar expands its tech contract. Overall sentiment is neutral to positive.

themes.title: Vendor contracts
themes.detail: Brightstar secured multiple extensions of the New York Lottery technology contract.

themes.title: Tech replacement
themes.detail: Light & Wonder was selected to replace Delaware North Table Games technology, indicating a shift in vendor landscape.

industries.it_note: Brightstar is expanding its IT spend, while other firms show unclear or neutral outlooks.

industries.summary: Pearson posted $1,779 m revenue with a 14.2% margin, while Scholastic missed revenue at $216.8 m and posted a -42.5% margin. Wolters Kluwer made no financial disclosures but added AI tools.

laggards.why: Revenue miss and deep operating loss

themes.title: AI integration
themes.detail: Wolters Kluwer and Pearson both embedded AI into their product suites, targeting tax, accounting and learning workflows.

themes.title: M&A activity
themes.detail: Scholastic announced a $71 m acquisition of Cottage Door Press.

industries.it_note: AI investments are evident, but overall IT spend outlook is not clearly defined.

industries.summary: Pearson continues revenue growth, NYU secured multi‑hundred‑million dollar quantum funding, and SLU expanded its AI partnership with World Wide Technology. ACT reported no major changes.

leaders.why: Strong revenue growth and AI‑focused product launches

laggards.why: No financial data or notable initiatives reported

themes.title: Quantum and AI research
themes.detail: NYU received $284 m for a quantum fabrication facility and $30 m for a quantum lab, while also applying AI to archaeology.

themes.title: Industry partnerships
themes.detail: SLU deepened its AI collaboration with World Wide Technology, adding branding to university jerseys.

industries.it_note: NYU’s quantum projects suggest expanding tech spend; other institutions show unclear or neutral IT outlooks.
